The S-N curve (stress vs cycles to failure) shows the safe stress limit below which fatigue is negligible. This is why railway axles must be inspected and discarded after a certain mileage even if they still look sound.

nodes.name: Fire assay for ore grade
nodes.note: Heat crushed ore in a cupel with lead, the base metals oxidize and are absorbed into the cupel, leaving a bead of precious metals. Works only if you understand that lead's affinity for impurities is the trick, and must be done at scale to check ore grade before large smelts. The assayer is the gatekeeper.

nodes.name: Froth flotation ore concentration
nodes.note: Grind ore to powder, mix with water and a collector chemical that makes valuable mineral surfaces hydrophobic. Bubble air through; mineral clings to bubbles and floats, waste sinks. This is non-obvious: you are separating by surface chemistry, not density. It transforms marginal ores into viable ones and is the one process that changed the definition of ore grade in the 20th century. Needs constant chemical supply.

nodes.name: Galvanizing with zinc coating
nodes.note: Dip clean iron into molten zinc. Zinc bonds metallurgically to iron and protects it from rust. The zinc-iron interface layer is hard and brittle; if you bend the bar sharply right after galvanizing it spalls and exposes the iron. Needs a pickling step with acid to remove rust and oxide before the dip, and flux (powdered chloride) to prevent oxidation of the zinc.

nodes.name: Green sand molding for casting
nodes.note: Damp sand mixed with clay is packed around a wooden pattern and fired gently to harden the mold without drying it out completely. The trapped water flashes to steam when molten metal enters, creating a small gap and preventing fusion. Cheap and fast but produces rough castings. Rome has this baseline method.

nodes.name: Hardenability and alloy steel design
nodes.note: Adding chromium, nickel, molybdenum, or vanadium increases the depth to which a steel can be hardened. Thick bars that quench-harden only to the surface need alloy addition to harden through. Hardenability is separate from hardness—a hard steel is not necessarily hardenable to depth. Engineers design alloys to achieve both the hardness and the through-hardening needed for large bearings and gears.

nodes.name: Hardness testing and Rockwell scale
nodes.note: Press a hardened indenter (diamond pyramid or steel ball) into the metal under a known load, measure the impression size. Larger impressions mean softer metal. Rockwell scale standardizes the test so results are comparable across labs. Fast and non-destructive, so useful for acceptance testing. Gives a single number but does not reveal structure or ductility.

nodes.name: Hydraulic press and accumulator
nodes.note: A pump driven by steam fills a cylinder with oil; the incompressible oil presses a ram with immense steady force. An accumulator (air-charged vessel) smooths pulsation and stores energy. Pascal's law means a small pump can generate large forces through a large piston. The limit is seal quality and pipe strength; if oil leaks you lose pressure instantly.

nodes.name: Investment casting and lost wax
nodes.note: Carve fine details in wax, embed in clay and sand, fire to melt and drive out the wax, pour molten metal into the cavity. Results in intricate castings with no parting lines. Rome has this for jewelry. For large castings it becomes expensive in wax and labor but the precision is unmatched. The name investment refers to the clay-sand shell that receives the investment. [AUDIT: capability prerequisite(s) cap_heat_0700 were inferred by rome/sim/treetool.py repair, not stated by the author. Treat them as a floor, not a specification.]

nodes.name: Jigging and gravity separation
nodes.note: Shake crushed ore in a slurry in a funnel-bottomed box; dense ore sinks, waste rock suspends and overflows. The real work is tuning the shake frequency and water flow—too fast and you lose ore, too slow and waste carries through. This becomes faster and cheaper than hand sorting at scale.

nodes.name: Mannesmann piercing for seamless tube
nodes.note: Two conical rolls rotating towards each other pierce a heated bar and push the center material outward. Sounds impossible but works because the material is plastic when hot and the geometry of the rolls forces flow. The innovation is recognizing that the centerline is in pure tension and will fail there, opening a hole. This is a non-obvious geometric fact.

nodes.name: Metallography: polishing, etching and microscopy
nodes.note: Polish a section of steel to mirror smoothness, etch with dilute acid to reveal grain boundaries and phases, look through a microscope. The microstructure tells you if the heat treatment worked, if the segregation is acceptable, if cracks are present. This single instrument—the microscope—transformed metallurgy from craft to science. No expensive equipment needed: a microscope and an etchant are sufficient.

nodes.name: Mine pumping systems
nodes.note: Use water power to drive a Cornish engine or a Newcomen atmospheric engine, then a force pump lifts water from the lowest level. Deep mines fill with water faster than hand bailing can remove it. The pumping plant is the largest single capital expense of a deep mine—without it, you cannot go deeper than about 100 meters. The pump must run constantly during operations.

nodes.name: Normalizing for uniformity
nodes.note: Heat to redness and cool in still air. Not as soft as full annealing but grain is fine and uniform. Normalizing after forging relieves working stress and prepares the metal for hardening or final machining. The open air cooling means no fuel cost for the cool-down phase. Used after every significant deformation to reset the structure.

nodes.name: Open hearth furnace and scrap recycling
nodes.note: A large reverberatory basin where you can melt pig iron, scrap, and iron ore together at controlled temperatures. Much slower than a converter but gives you time to remove impurities chemically. The furnace can recycle scrap and burnt parts that a converter wastes. Fuel cost is higher but flexibility is the gain.

nodes.name: Ore dressing: crushing and hand sorting
nodes.note: Breaking ore by hand and gravity-separating visible rich and waste rock is unchanged since antiquity. The skill is recognizing which rock will pay: this is entirely empirical and learned from the ground itself. Rome needs labour, not invention.

nodes.name: Oxy-acetylene welding and brazing
nodes.note: A flame from acetylene and oxygen burning at 3000 K melts both the filler rod and the parent metal, joining them. Works on steel, copper, and aluminum. The flame is small and precisely controllable, so you can weld thin sheet or repair castings. Safety requires careful regulator tuning: reverse flow into acetylene generator causes explosion. The acetylene supply infrastructure is the bottleneck.

nodes.name: Iron-carbon phase diagram as scientific knowledge
nodes.note: Map the regions of phase stability as a function of temperature and carbon content. Shows transformation temperatures (critical points where austenite, ferrite, cementite appear or vanish). This transforms blacksmith's empirical heat-color craft into predictable science. The diagram is the foundation of all intelligent steel making; without it you are working blind even if your hands are skilled.

nodes.name: Pneumatic rock drill
nodes.note: A small piston driven by compressed air strikes a hardened bit repeatedly against rock, advancing into the hole while the operator rotates it slightly between blows. Drills much faster than hand drilling with hammer and chisel. The air compressor must be driven by steam and the hose is heavy and expensive. Enables deep blast holes that hand drilling never could achieve, transforming mining efficiency.

nodes.name: Powder metallurgy and sintering
nodes.note: Tungsten cannot be melted and cast (melting point 3420 C). The only path to a tungsten object is: powder, press into a shape under high pressure, then sinter (heat just below melting at high temperature in a hydrogen atmosphere) to bond the particles. This is the sole way to make tungsten into anything usable. The sintered part is porous and brittle until you press it again.

nodes.name: Quenching media and quench crack prevention
nodes.note: Cool speed determines hardness: fast quench in water is maximum hardness but causes cracks, slow quench in oil is lower hardness but safer. The quench crack forms because the surface hardens and shrinks while the core is still hot and soft, creating tensile stress. Brine quenches faster than water. Control of temperature drop rate is the art. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Rail mill production
nodes.note: Roll steel billets into the precise section and straightness demanded by railways. Straight track depends on rails within tolerance. The section mill can produce the profile but the end straightness and the weld joint (joining two rails end-to-end) are where most waste happens. Needs close process control and sorting of bad rails.

nodes.name: Resistance welding and spot welding
nodes.note: Clamp the work between two copper electrodes and pass current through it. Resistance heating melts a small zone where the overlap is, forming a weld nugget. Works only on sheet metal and thin stock. No filler, no gas, fast and clean. The electrodes must be soft copper with high conductivity or they overheat and wear. Spot welding revolutionized automotive body assembly.

nodes.name: Reverberatory furnace
nodes.note: The charge sits on the hearth, flames from a separate firebox bounce off an arched roof and melt the metal. Fuel never touches the charge—this is the crucial difference from a blast furnace. Enables puddling and copper refining because slag does not contaminate with coke ash. The roof must be shaped right or it cracks under thermal shock.

nodes.name: Reversing rolling mill
nodes.note: Motor reverses direction between passes. Steel goes through in one direction, emerges, is turned, fed back through in the opposite direction. Allows many passes at speed without the labour of flipping. Electric motor with reversing controller is essential; a steam engine cannot reverse fast enough without danger.

nodes.name: Roasting and calcining ore
nodes.note: Heat ore in an open pile to drive off volatile sulfur and water, and to crack the rock for easier reduction. Many sulfide ores cannot be smelted without roasting first; the roast fumes are toxic. Needs a scholar to understand stoichiometry or roasters waste half their ore.

nodes.name: Safety lamps and mine ventilation
nodes.note: A closed lamp with a wire gauze that absorbs heat from a methane flame, cooling it below the ignition point, so the flame does not ignite the gas in the mine but you can still see the methane by the color change. Water-driven ventilation fans push air into the mine through one shaft while another shaft lets stale air escape. Both are essential: the lamp tells you gas is present, the ventilation dilutes it to safe levels.

nodes.name: Section mill for rails and beams
nodes.note: Rolls are shaped to press the bar into a desired section: I-beam, T-rail, angle iron. Each pass uses different rolls, so the bar gradually forms. Temperature control is critical because the metal must be plastic enough to flow into the roll valleys without tearing. Very high forces mean the rolls must be backed by strong housings or they will sag and kill accuracy.

nodes.name: Spectroscopic assay of metals
nodes.note: Excite a metal sample with an electric spark and analyze the light with a spectroscope. Each element produces specific lines; the intensity tells you concentration. Fast and requires minimal sample preparation. Can be done in the foundry during a heat to verify alloy composition before pouring. The spark gap must be precisely positioned and the spectroscope aligned or results scatter wildly.

nodes.name: Steam hammer for precision forging
nodes.note: Steam cylinder pushes the hammer down instead of dropping it. You control force and speed with the steam valve, not gravity, so you can forge delicate shapes without cracking. Far more work per hour than a drop hammer. The hazard is that steam can fail suddenly and the hammer drops uncontrolled; strong dies and guides are essential.

nodes.name: Tempering and temper color chart
nodes.note: Heat hardened steel to a lower temperature to relieve quench stress and reduce brittleness. The temperature is judged by the surface oxide color: pale straw, brown, dark blue. Too low a temper leaves it brittle, too high softens it too much. Color tempering is a visual art that has been refined over centuries. The temper color chart is portable and teachable knowledge.

nodes.name: Tensile testing and the testing machine
nodes.note: Grip a specimen in a powered machine, pull it apart, measure the load and elongation. Plot load vs elongation to find yield strength, ultimate strength, and elongation to failure. The testing machine must pull at constant rate with a load cell accurate to 1 percent or the data is worthless. This data is the only way to verify that specifications are being met; without tests you cannot know if a batch of steel is good.

nodes.name: Three-high rolling mill
nodes.note: Three rolls arranged so the middle roll reverses between passes. Bar goes down between bottom and middle, then back up between middle and top, then down again. Doubles throughput without a reversing mechanism. The middle roll is under enormous load from both sides and must be extraordinarily hard or it will deflect and produce bad gauging.

nodes.name: Tin plate production
nodes.note: Electroplate iron sheet with tin or dip into molten tin. Tin is non-toxic and corrosion-resistant, so tinned steel is ideal for food storage. The tin coating must be continuous or rust starts at the pin-holes. Electroplated tin plate is thinner and cheaper than dipped; dipped is thicker but more durable. The difference is in the tin-iron bond strength.

nodes.name: Trip hammer and water-driven forge hammer
nodes.note: A cam on a water wheel shaft lifts a heavy hammer, then the cam releases it and gravity and the impact do the forging work. Much faster than hand hammering and the work is uniform. The key is that the head must be hard iron or the repeated impact will deform it; case-hardening is necessary to survive. Rome has this; it is the foundation of heavy forge work.

nodes.name: Tube mill and seamless tube production
nodes.note: A seamless tube that holds pressure is the only solution for hydraulics and high-pressure steam. Mannesmann's innovation: two rotating conical rolls pierce the center of a heated bar as it passes between them, then a sizing mandrel expands the hole and the formed tube to size. Requires precise balance and speed control; one roll wobble ruins the batch. The seamless tube transformed high-pressure technology.

nodes.name: Two-high rolling mill
nodes.note: Two iron rolls, one fixed, one movable, crush hot steel bar between them. The bar emerges thinner and longer. Needs rolls of sufficient hardness and a power source that does not stall under load—cast iron rolls are barely adequate and shatter under shock; hardened steel rolls are better but hard to make. The steel must be hot enough to flow without cracking. Getting the temperature, roll gap, and feed speed in balance is an art.

nodes.name: Water-powered ore stamp mill
nodes.note: Cam-driven stamps powered by a water wheel crush ore in a mortar far faster than hand crushing. The bottleneck is the cam and the hardness of the iron stamp-heads. Needs high-carbon iron or case-hardened steel. This is where labour-displacement troubles the guild.

nodes.name: Winding engine and mine shaft hoisting
nodes.note: A steam engine driving a large reel with steel wire rope hoists ore and workers from depth. The rope must be wire, not hemp, or it breaks under load and falls into the shaft. The brake must hold the maximum load suspended or a rope failure is a catastrophe. Regular inspections for wear and fraying are essential; a frayed rope is a widow-maker.

nodes.name: Wire rod rolling mill
nodes.note: A series of small oval and round rolls progressively thins a bar into coiled wire rod, which is then drawn to final size. The wire emerges hot and coils as it cools. The speed is high—modern mills run at meters per second—so you need strong power and excellent roll material or the rolls will crack and scatter pieces. A single roll failure at speed can cause line shutdown for a day.

nodes.name: Micrometer, verniers, gauge blocks, go/no-go gauges
nodes.note: Measurement precedes manufacture. Publish your standards and distribute copies of the master gauges to every workshop you fund, or your parts will not interchange between cities.

nodes.name: Compound microscope with achromatic objective
nodes.note: Do not build this before the bead microscope. A bad compound instrument is worse than a good single lens, which is exactly why van Leeuwenhoek won for fifty years. Needs lead flint glass for the achromatic doublet.

nodes.name: Mineral concessions and access to imperial mines
nodes.note: Mercury (Almaden) and much else is an imperial monopoly. Halves the cost of all ore and metal inputs thereafter.

nodes.name: Tin-mercury amalgam plate mirrors
nodes.note: Roman mirrors are small, dark and mostly polished bronze or lead-backed glass. A true plate mirror is a luxury good with an obscene margin. Mercury vapour will poison your workers; ventilate, rotate them, and do not let them eat in the shop.

nodes.name: Motors, transformers, alternating current
nodes.note: Laminate the cores or eddy currents will eat your efficiency and cook the iron. Three-phase and transformers make distribution possible, which is what turns a workshop generator into a grid. CALENDAR FLOOR is set by diffusion, not by construction: the economy needs roughly a generation to train the trades, form the capital and build the suppliers. Money cannot buy this down.

nodes.name: Newtonian mechanics and gravitation
nodes.note: Directly contradicts Aristotle in public, which is the expensive part. The astronomical predictions it makes are your proof and they are unanswerable. Publicly overturns Aristotle on motion. Make the case with predictions that cannot be argued with (planetary positions, pendulum periods, artillery trajectories) rather than with argument.

nodes.name: Nitre beds and potassium nitrate
nodes.note: START THIS IN MONTH ONE. It is the longest lead-time item in the tree: the beds take 12-24 months to mature no matter what you spend. Roman nitrum is sodium carbonate, not nitre; there is no saltpetre anywhere in the Roman economy. The non-obvious step is boiling the leachate with wood-ash potash to convert calcium nitrate to the potassium salt, which is the one that actually works. [AUDIT: capability prerequisite(s) cap_tol_100um were inferred by rome/sim/treetool.py repair, not stated by the author. Treat them as a floor, not a specification.]

nodes.name: Nitric acid
nodes.note: Saltpetre plus oil of vitriol, distilled. Unlocks aqua regia, silver nitrate (hence photography and silvered mirrors), etching, nitrates and, if you choose it, high explosives. The brown fumes will kill anyone who breathes them and the damage is delayed by hours.

nodes.name: Abbe condenser (microscope illuminator)
nodes.note: Lens system below stage converges light from source onto specimen at angle equal to objective's aperture. Numerical aperture must match objective. Huge effect on contrast and resolution.

nodes.name: Achromatic doublet lens
nodes.note: Crown and flint glass in contact correct chromatic aberration by choosing radii such that focal length is nearly independent of wavelength. Geometry demands extraordinary precision.

nodes.name: Anemometer (wind speed)
nodes.note: Three or four cups catch wind, spin axle. Pulses close switch or increment counter. Calibration against standard wind tunnel difficult; approximation from rotation rate works to 10 percent.

nodes.name: Aneroid barometer
nodes.note: Partial vacuum box with corrugated brass diaphragm. Spring restores motion calibrated to mercury barometer. No mercury; portable and linear. Hysteresis and dial friction require friction compensation. [AUDIT: capability prerequisite(s) cap_vac_1torr were inferred by rome/sim/treetool.py repair, not stated by the author. Treat them as a floor, not a specification.]

nodes.name: Apochromatic lens (three-glass)
nodes.note: Three glass elements correct chromatic aberration to smaller wavelength band than doublet, reducing false color to negligible in visual light. Requires flint and two crown varieties.

nodes.name: Artificial horizon for navigation
nodes.note: Mercury pool creates perfectly level reflecting surface. Sextant reflection doubled. Allows altitude measurement by boat even in rough seas. Mercury maintenance and capsule risk.

nodes.name: Ballistic galvanometer (charge measurement)
nodes.note: Moving coil over-damped with long period. Charge dumps in short pulse; coil swings proportionally. Integral of current over time measured without recording. Detects magnetic flux changes.

nodes.name: Bolometer (radiation detector)
nodes.note: Thin platinum strip heated by incoming radiation, resistance change measured by bridge. Extremely sensitive but requires temperature control and isolation from air currents.

nodes.name: Bourdon pressure gauge
nodes.note: Oval brass tube coiled as helix; pressure forces straightening, rotates needle via linkage. Nonlinear response requires empirical dial calibration. Robust and field-durable.

nodes.name: Burning glass
nodes.note: Seneca describes how a globe of water can concentrate sunlight to ignite. Rome already possesses this effect; neither lens nor glass shaping needed, just geometry.

nodes.name: Calorimeter (heat capacity apparatus)
nodes.note: Insulated container of water. Add fuel or material, measure temperature rise. Specific heat calculated from mass and T change. Precision limited by insulation imperfection.

nodes.name: Chronograph (time marker)
nodes.note: Vibrating tuning fork marks dots on paper tape at 100 Hz. Paper moves at known speed, displacement read in milliseconds. Measures bullet transit time and explosives detonation intervals.

nodes.name: Clock drive for telescope tracking
nodes.note: Escapement-driven gear train rotates telescope at sidereal rate (slightly slower than solar rate). Accuracy to seconds per night demands temperature stability.

nodes.name: Diffraction grating
nodes.note: Tens of thousands of parallel lines 1 micron apart. Diffraction by equal spacing separates spectrum by wavelength more uniformly than prism. Made by ruling engine only.

nodes.name: Dioptra (sighting tube)
nodes.note: Tube with sights at each end (no lens) measures angles to distant marks. Hero describes gear-driven versions.

nodes.name: Electrometer (charge measurement)
nodes.note: Galvanometer with high input impedance measures small currents from charged object. Quadrant electrometer achieves 1e-9 ampere sensitivity by using torque rather than deflection.

nodes.name: Electron microscope
nodes.note: Filament heated to emission in vacuum, electrons accelerated through 10-100 kV, focused by magnetic coils acting as lenses. Wavelength 0.1 nm allows 1 nm resolution. Requires bakeable vacuum chamber and careful filament life.

nodes.name: Equatorial telescope mount
nodes.note: One axis tilted parallel to Earth's axis. Rotating that axis alone keeps object centered as Earth spins. Requires precise latitude calculation and mechanical balance.

nodes.name: Flame and spark spectra for element assay
nodes.note: Spark or flame emitted through sample salt identifies element by line pattern. Replaces classical wet analysis for many ores and minerals. Fast but requires reference samples.

nodes.name: Focal length measurement
nodes.note: Form image of distant sun or window on screen, measure distance from lens to sharp image. Elementary but requires careful measurement and shielding from wind vibration.

nodes.name: Fraunhofer lines catalog
nodes.note: Mapping dark lines in solar spectrum and naming them by letter (H, K, D, etc). Over 500 lines exist. Requires years of careful observation and comparison with terrestrial sources.

nodes.name: Geared mechanical transmission
nodes.note: Bronze and iron gears with involute or cycloidal flanks transmit rotary motion at calculated ratios. The Antikythera mechanism shows Rome's capability.

nodes.name: Gravimeter (gravity field measurement)
nodes.note: Period of pendulum depends on local g. Measure period to 1 millisecond over many swings; gravity variations of 1 part in 1e6 detectable. Spring-based instruments avoid suspension issues.

nodes.name: Groma (surveying cross)
nodes.note: Four arms with plumb bobs hung from crosspiece establish right angles for land survey. Roman roads and centuriation owe their precision to this.

nodes.name: High speed camera
nodes.note: Multiple rotating drum with lenses or rotating mirror. Exposes film at 1000 frames per second. Shutter speed below 1 microsecond by mechanical or electrical gating. Film advance is challenge.

nodes.name: Hygrometer (humidity measurement)
nodes.note: Human hair lengthens and shortens with humidity (0-0.25 mm over 0-100 percent). Mechanical linkage magnifies to pointer on dial. Requires calibration by salt solutions.

nodes.name: Optical level (surveying)
nodes.note: Telescope with bubble level establishes horizontal. Staff markings read through telescope. Detects height difference to 1 mm at 100 meters. Pendulum-damped level improves stability.

nodes.name: Magnetometer (magnetic field measurement)
nodes.note: Magnetic needle deflects in field, angle measured against scale. Compass declination survey maps Earth's field; horizontal and vertical components separated by orientation changes.

nodes.name: Manometer (pressure measurement)
nodes.note: U-tube with mercury. Pressure difference raises one column, depresses other. Read in mm Hg directly. Linearity to better than 1 percent across range 0-2 atm.

nodes.name: Polished metal mirror
nodes.note: Bronze and silver polished to reflect. Rome makes excellent mirrors; the technology is established.

nodes.name: Michelson interferometer
nodes.note: Split beam into two perpendicular paths, recombine, count fringes. Moving mirror one wavelength shifts fringes by two. Can measure distances to 0.1 micron. Requires rigid frame and ambient vibration isolation.

nodes.name: Newton's rings interference pattern
nodes.note: Lens resting on flat glass shows concentric rings where air gap equals integer wavelengths. Wavelength of light can be computed from ring spacing. Elegant proof that light has finite wavelength.

nodes.name: Nicol prism for polarized light
nodes.note: Calcite (Iceland spar) crystal cut and cemented at Brewster angle passes one polarization. Extraordinary ray refracted 90 degrees, separated by cement into wasted beam. Alignment precise to 1 degree.

nodes.name: Oil immersion microscope objective
nodes.note: Oil between coverslip and lens increases numerical aperture. Requires lens design change and oil choice for index match. Cleaning lens after use is non-trivial; oil hardens if heated.

nodes.name: Oscilloscope (CRT time-display)
nodes.note: Cathode ray tube, beam deflected by time-base and signal voltages. Traces waveform directly on screen. Requires 1000+ volt HT supply and precise synchronization.

nodes.name: Phase contrast microscopy
nodes.note: Condenser annulus and objective phase plate convert invisible phase shifts (from transparent cells) into visible amplitude changes. Reveals internal structure without stain. Requires precise centering.

nodes.name: Photocell (photoelectric detector)
nodes.note: Cesium or other photoemissive surface in vacuum emits electrons when light strikes. Current amplified by dynamo or triode. Single photon detectable in dark conditions.

nodes.name: Photometry and light measurement
nodes.note: Compare brightness of standard candles by visual contrast or disk photometer. Requires calibrated sources and standard atmospheric conditions. Historically done by Rumford.

nodes.name: Pitot tube (fluid velocity)
nodes.note: Two tubes: one faces flow (stagnation pressure), one is tangent (static pressure). Difference measured by manometer. Velocity = sqrt(2*g*h). Requires smooth entry and minimal blockage.

nodes.name: Plane table surveying
nodes.note: Telescope mounted on wooden board over map. Sighting to features and drawing lines produces map directly. Faster than theodolite but less precise; good for topographic detail.

nodes.name: Plano-convex reading lens
nodes.note: A flat surface facing text, one curved. Magnification roughly equals curvature radius divided by focal length. The blower must hold perfect sphere while cooling.

nodes.name: Polarimeter for optical rotation
nodes.note: Light polarized by first Nicol passes through sample solution. Analyzer (second Nicol) rotated until extinction. Rotation angle tells sugar concentration. Sweet plant validation of physics.

nodes.name: Potentiometer (precision voltage measurement)
nodes.note: Known voltage (from standard cell) balanced against unknown via null galvanometer. Sliding contact on calibrated wire determines ratio. Zero-current measurement avoids galvanic heating.

nodes.name: Pyrometer by rod contraction
nodes.note: Metal rod held at measurement site cools slowly, shrinkage measured mechanically. Each alloy has known contraction rate; calibration by known temperature control required.

nodes.name: Pyrometer by color (optical)
nodes.note: Spectral lines of tungsten filament shifted in position compared to heated object. Brightness match at one wavelength determines temperature. Requires calibration filament and dark room.

nodes.name: Pyrometer by radiation (Stefan-Boltzmann)
nodes.note: Lens focuses radiation from hot object onto bolometer or photocell. Power proportional to T^4. Non-contact measurement but requires emissivity correction and accurate focus.

nodes.name: Pyrometer by thermocouple
nodes.note: Two dissimilar metals joined; junction heated, voltage measured by galvanometer. Nonlinear but reproducible. Platinum-rhodium allows temperatures to 1600 C.

nodes.name: Reflecting telescope (Newtonian)
nodes.note: Curved mirror of polished speculum focuses light; flat secondary deflects beam to eyepiece at side. Avoids chromatic aberration but requires frequent re-polishing.

nodes.name: Refractometer (Abbe design)
nodes.note: Sample between two prisms; critical angle marks boundary between dark and light regions. Scales directly in refractive index. Determines salt concentration and purity of liquids.

nodes.name: Ruling engine for grating production
nodes.note: Machine whose sole purpose is scratching tens of thousands of equally spaced lines. Demands the finest lead screw in existence, thermal stability to microns, diamond tool, and 2 years of debugging.

nodes.name: Seismograph (earthquake measurement)
nodes.note: Heavy mass damped by springs or pendulum. Frame sits on ground. Relative motion drives pen against rotating drum. Natural period of 10-20 seconds maximizes sensitivity to distant earthquakes.

nodes.name: Sextant for angle measurement
nodes.note: Arc of 60 degrees, mirror and telescope measure angle to horizon. Tangent screw with vernier scale reads to 1 arcminute. At sea, determines latitude directly from sun or star altitude.

nodes.name: Silvered glass mirror for telescope
nodes.note: Silver or mercury amalgam coated to glass substrate. More reflive than speculum and lasts longer between recleaning, but coating is fragile. Glass must be flat to better than 1 micron.

nodes.name: Spectacles (eyeglasses)
nodes.note: Two lenses mounted in a frame to correct presbyopia or myopia. Suspicion arises because it appears to grant unnatural vision. Matching a pair requires testing many lenses.

nodes.name: Spectroheliograph (solar spectrograph)
nodes.note: Spectroscope coupled to telescope with narrow slit selects one wavelength from solar disk, mapping Sun in single element lines (H-alpha shows chromosphere structure). Requires perfect collimation.

nodes.name: Spectroscopy: absorption line method
nodes.note: White light through cool gas shows dark lines where gas absorbs. Same elements produce same line positions. The complement of emission; requires bright background source.

nodes.name: Spectroscopy: emission line method
nodes.note: Heated element emits spectrum of lines, each element distinct. Allows identification of what is burning. Requires catalog of known lines and careful temperature control.

nodes.name: Speculum metal for telescope mirror
nodes.note: Copper-tin alloy with trace arsenic becomes hard and reflective. Cooling rate and composition affect color and tarnish rate. British Museum alloys show trial-and-error over decades.

nodes.name: Spherometer for curvature measurement
nodes.note: Three legs at radius R, central screw measures sag of curved surface. Radius of curvature is computed from sag formula. Template surfaces act as control standard for grinding.

nodes.name: Standards laboratory as institution
nodes.note: Building, personnel, standards, and equipment to maintain national measures. Meter bar, kilogram weight, temperature scale, density standards. Traceability requires stability and isolation from vibration.

nodes.name: Steelyard balance
nodes.note: Unequal arms with movable weight on calibrated beam weighs goods without counter-weights. Rome has this; precision limited to roughly 1 percent.

nodes.name: Stellar parallax and arcsecond precision
nodes.note: Star shifts position by one arcsecond from opposite ends of Earth's orbit if within ~3 light-years. Measurement demands micrometer precision, patience, and stable telescope. First measured by Bessel in 1838.

nodes.name: Stroboscope (periodic light)
nodes.note: Rotating disk or electric lamp flash synchronized to object rotation freezes motion. Variable frequency allows measuring RPM directly. Spectator error (aliasing) common.

nodes.name: Sundial
nodes.note: Shadow cast by the gnomon measures hour angle. Rome has precise designs based on latitude.

nodes.name: Theodolite (transit and altitude)
nodes.note: Telescope on two perpendicular pivots with graduated circles. Vernier scale reads horizontal and vertical angles to arcminute. Foundation of triangulation and mapping.

nodes.name: Transit instrument (meridian telescope)
nodes.note: Telescope pivots only in east-west, fixed in north-south. When star crosses meridian, exact time and altitude determine latitude and star position. Requires mercury basin for latitude check.

nodes.name: Ultramicroscope (dark field)
nodes.note: Slit illuminator sends light at grazing angle past objective aperture. Particles too small to resolve by normal microscopy (Tyndall effect) scatter light into objective as bright specs. Reveals colloid and virus sizes.

nodes.name: Water clock (clepsydra)
nodes.note: Steady flow of water through orifice marks time independent of sky. Rome perfected this and added geared indicator dials.

nodes.name: Water-filled globe as magnifier
nodes.note: Spherical water containers magnify. The phenomenon is ancient and refraction geometry tells you why.

nodes.name: Imperial patronage
nodes.note: Approach through the a rationibus or the Praetorian Prefect, not the emperor. The optical telegraph is the demonstration that buys this: an empire's core problem is that a message to the Rhine takes weeks. Unlocks mining concessions, corvee labour and state funding, and puts a target on you.

nodes.name: Secure a town patron
nodes.note: Cheapest entry gift is a pair of reading lenses for an ageing magistrate. Halves incoming suspicion.

nodes.name: Senatorial patronage
nodes.note: Bought with a cure, a profit, or a public benefaction in their name. Pliny the Younger's circle is the target type.

nodes.name: Silver halide photography on glass
nodes.note: Not a luxury, an instrument. It records spectra, star positions, metal microstructure, and eventually a photolithographic mask. It will also look more like sorcery than anything else you do, so introduce it via portraiture of the powerful, who will forgive anything that flatters them.

nodes.name: Quarantine, clean water, sanitation and variolation programme
nodes.note: You know the Antonine Plague arrives in 165 AD. This node is what decides whether your institute survives it. Highest expected-value defensive investment in the game. It is also the thing most likely to be called sorcery, so do it under a patron and in public. [AUDIT: capability prerequisite(s) cap_tol_100um were inferred by rome/sim/treetool.py repair, not stated by the author. Treat them as a floor, not a specification.]

nodes.name: Point-contact transistor
nodes.note: THE GOAL. An n-type germanium slab with two phosphor bronze points a fraction of a millimetre apart, plus a forming pulse. Fragile, noisy, irreproducible and it amplifies. Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley, December 1947. Getting here from 100 AD is the whole game.

nodes.name: Potash, caustic potash, soda and caustic soda
nodes.note: Rome has natron in bulk from Egypt and wood ash everywhere. Causticising with slaked lime is the step they do not take. Feeds soap, glass and the nitre beds.

nodes.name: Central generation and distribution
nodes.note: The precondition for every energy-intensive process that follows: arc furnaces, electrolysis, aluminium, and the sustained laboratory power a semiconductor programme consumes. This is a civilisational-scale project, not a workshop one. CALENDAR FLOOR is set by diffusion, not by construction: the economy needs roughly a generation to train the trades, form the capital and build the suppliers. Money cannot buy this down.

nodes.name: Apprentice system and skill transfer in toolmaking
nodes.note: Boy apprenticed at 12, bound for 7 years. Learns by doing under master guidance. Picks up tacit knowledge (feel for scraper, reading dial indicator) that cannot be written down. Replaces each master with successor. Lineal transfer of craft.

nodes.name: Arbor press for bearing and gear installation
nodes.note: Screw-driven ram applies steady pressure (up to 5 tonnes). Arbors (hardened tapers) support work true to mandrel. Enables interference fits (bearing on shaft) and gear assembly without hammer risk. Repeatability to 1mm.

nodes.name: Autocollimator for angle and parallelism measurement
nodes.note: Telescope with reticule and light source reflects light off target mirror. Tilt changes reflected spot on reticule. Each 1mm spot shift = 3 arc-seconds tilt. Enables checking machine tool bed parallelism and spindle axis alignment to 1 arc-second.

nodes.name: Automatic screw machine with cams and limit stops
nodes.note: Driven by steam motor. Cams and trip dogs sequence tool operations and advance work. Completely unattended running once set. Operator knowledge needed is minimal: just threading the magazine. Scares artisans. Requires skilled cam grinder and cap_tol_100um stops.

nodes.name: Back-gear reduction drive
nodes.note: Gear train engaged by clutch reverses spindle direction and reduces speed 3:1 to 5:1. Allows heavy roughing and soft brasses without exceeding foot speed. Teeth cut by hand with gear cutter or master cutter. Enables slow steady feeds on long work.

nodes.name: Ball and roller bearing with precision grinding
nodes.note: Spheres or cylinders ground to 1 micron roundness require automated grinding. Races (inner/outer rings) ground to 10 micron form. Preload and clearance adjusted to limit axial play to 5 microns. Enables spindle speeds 5000+ rpm at 10 micron runout.

nodes.name: Ballscrew with recirculating balls and 0.01mm backlash
nodes.note: Balls recirculate in helical groove, not sliding friction. Backlash under 0.01mm, no stick-slip. Thread ground to 0.05mm accuracy; ball-raceway hardness (Rc 58+) matches bearing races. Five-fold speed increase and zero runout drift compared to lead screw.

nodes.name: Broach tool and broaching machine
nodes.note: Long bar with progressive teeth (each 0.1mm taller) pulled or pushed through hole or across surface. Removes complex profile in one stroke. Requires 0.05mm tooth accuracy and strong machine frame. Enables keyways, splines, and precision slots.

nodes.name: Capstan and turret lathe
nodes.note: Turret holds 6-8 tools indexed by hand. Capstan (large handwheel) feeds work to preset stops. Repeatable positioning requires mechanical stops accurate to 0.1mm. Unskilled operator can repeat production. Massive labour saving, hence state interest.

nodes.name: Change gears and quadrant for automatic feed
nodes.note: Interchangeable gear pairs couple spindle to lead screw. Quadrant index positions gears. Swapping gears changes feed rate and thread pitch. Gear ratios must maintain thread lead precision, so gears need cutting accuracy 0.1mm pitch. Eliminates hand-wheel cranking.

nodes.name: Optical comparator for part profiling
nodes.note: Overhead lens projects magnified silhouette (30x to 100x) onto screen. Operator aligns part edge to master outline. Enables rapid profile checking and sorting of gears, cams, and punch dies. Fast but less accurate than dial indicator.

nodes.name: Compound slide rest with two lead screws
nodes.note: Cross-slide mounted on top of longitudinal slide, also driven by lead screw. Enables angled cuts and conical threads. Compound angle reduces tangential cutting error. Requires two independent lead screws or gebraic linkage, both needing cap_tol_100um threads.

nodes.name: Coolant and cutting fluid for speed and finish
nodes.note: Sulphurized oil reduces friction 50%, cutting speed 2x. Coolant (water-soluble) prevents thermal expansion error. Turpentine or kerosene for aluminium. Each material has optimal formulation. Enables closer tolerances by heat control.

nodes.name: Cylindrical grinder for external and internal
nodes.note: Work spindle rotates; abrasive wheel feeds radially. Wheel can work OD, ID, or both. Requires cap_tol_10um spindle bearings and table feed. Enables bearing journals and piston fit bores to 10 microns.

nodes.name: Cylindrical square for checking bores
nodes.note: Cylinder ground to 0.01mm runout. Inserted into bore; any deviation from perpendicularity shows as rocking. Enables checking cylinder squareness to axis at 0.1mm per metre. Precision depends on grind quality.

nodes.name: Depth gauge with vernier for holes and recesses
nodes.note: Vernier scale mounted on sliding rod. Parallel base sits on part surface, rod projects down into recess. Measures depth to 0.05mm. Enables depth control in drilling and recessing operations.

nodes.name: Dial indicator with 0.01mm resolution
nodes.note: Plunger moves gear-driven pointer over dial. 10 mm plunge motion maps to 100 mm dial rotation, enabling 0.01mm readability. Mechanical magnification via gearing. Enables spindle runout and table flatness checking.

nodes.name: Die sinker and electrode erosion
nodes.note: Graphite or copper electrode sinks cavity into hardened steel by electrical discharge (arcing in oil). No contact: cuts hardened steel without work-hardening. Enables complex cavities (watch cases, bearing races) without hand scraping. Accuracy 0.1mm; finish poor but suitable for forging dies.

nodes.name: Dividing head for indexing and spiral milling
nodes.note: Spindle indexed via worm gear (ratio 40:1). Index plate with holes and sector arms set the angle. Enables cutting gears, cams, and helical grooves. Accuracy depends on worm gear backlash (must be <0.05mm at spindle) and hole spacing precision (0.1mm).

nodes.name: Drill press with feed screw and depth stop
nodes.note: Spindle rotates on precision bearings. Feed screw lowers drill into work at controlled rate. Stop blocks set depth repeatably to 1mm. Eliminates hand-pressure variation and dangerous walk. Enables accurate hole spacing in jigs.

nodes.name: Fly cutter for large flat faces
nodes.note: Single cutting tool offset on rotating radius. Covers large area with single spiral pass. Slow but saves time on facing big castings. Tip must be brazed and ground to 0.1mm flatness. Enables facing of casting parting surfaces.

nodes.name: Gauge blocks and wringing with 0.5 micron accuracy
nodes.note: Hardened steel blocks ground to 0.5 micron accuracy. Wringing (sliding together under pressure) removes air film, blocks stick by molecular force. Stacking 5-6 blocks builds any length. Enables checking micrometer accuracy and jig boring positions. Game-changer for interchangeable manufacturing.

nodes.name: Go-no-go gauges for production sorting
nodes.note: Two gauges: 'go' is at tolerance max, 'no-go' at min. Part passes both or is scrapped. Requires gauge block accuracy for calibration. Unskilled worker can sort: one part per second. Cost is high precision gauge cost; labour cost drops to near-zero.

nodes.name: Honing machine for cylinder bores
nodes.note: Multiple small honing stones in rotating mandrel cut on expansion, removing 0.002 to 0.005 inch (50-125 micron) from bore. Produces 0.5 micron finish and 0.01mm roundness. Critical for engine cylinders and hydraulic actuators.

nodes.name: Jig and fixture for interchangeable manufacture
nodes.note: Jig: guides drill to accuracy. Fixture: clamps part to machine table concentrically. Both require 0.01mm bore and datum alignment. Jigs for gun parts (musket locks) were state-of-art 1815. Enables unskilled labour to make parts to spec.

nodes.name: Jig boring machine with precision spindle
nodes.note: Spindle runout <0.002 inches (50 microns) via precision bearings. Quill feed screw cuts jig holes to 0.01mm location in cast castings. Dial indicator on spindle measures hole position to 0.01mm. Enables mass production of interchangeable jigs and tooling.

nodes.name: Lapping with cast-iron plate and abrasive compound
nodes.note: Emery and oil rubbed on massive cast-iron plate removes 1-10 microns and polishes to 0.5 micron finish. Flat lapping generates three-plate flatness automatically. Slow: 1mm removal per hour. Essential after grinding to remove burr and achieve optical quality.

nodes.name: Lathe faceplate and driving plates
nodes.note: Cast-iron plate bolts to spindle nose; work bolts to plate. Hand-scraped face ensures coplanarity to 1mm. Without it, work runout is uncontrolled. Enables chucking of large irregular work.

nodes.name: Lead screw error correction cam and follower
nodes.note: Grinding a lead screw leaves periodic runout (0.05mm). Measuring runout and grinding a cam follower that compensates enables 0.01mm lead accuracy. Follower attached to tool post cancels runout. Expensive, rarely done. Enables perfect pitch on long lead screws.

nodes.name: Machine frame and cast iron for damping vibration
nodes.note: Grey cast iron: internal friction dampens vibration better than steel. Massive frame (500+ kg) lowers resonant frequency below spindle speed. Chatter (0.01mm ripple at 500 Hz) ruins finish and shortens tool life. Frame design is as important as spindle accuracy.

nodes.name: Mandrel and self-centering chuck
nodes.note: The mandrel supports rotating spindles; the chuck holds work concentrically. Requires conical taper fitting and 1mm hand-scraped seating. Enables repeatable centering without re-marking.

nodes.name: Climate-controlled metrology room at 20 Celsius
nodes.note: 20 Celsius is reference; 1 degree change changes steel 0.01mm per metre. Granite surface plates on massive piers isolate from vibration. Ventilation removes body heat and light heat. Expensive, rare, but essential for 0.01mm accuracy. Most toolrooms ignore it, achieving 0.1mm instead.

nodes.name: Milling machine with rotating cutter
nodes.note: Rotating multi-flute cutter cuts on peripheral edges and end. Perpendicular feed removes vastly more material than planing. Requires spindle bearings accurate to 0.1mm runout and feed screws with matching tolerance. The spindle-bearing precision is the hard part.

nodes.name: Optical flat and Newton's rings for flatness
nodes.note: Thick glass plate ground flat within 0.2 microns. Monochromatic light creates Newton's rings: dark fringes show topography to 0.25 microns. Enables checking grinder wheel truing and lapping plate flatness. Only optical method for surface checking under 1 micron.

nodes.name: Pantograph and copying mechanism for die sinking
nodes.note: Stylus follows master template (wood or soft brass). Pantograph linkage (parallelogram with adjustable magnification) drives cutter at 1:1 or scaled. Enables reproducing intricate shapes (gun locks, coin dies). Requires mechanical accuracy to 1mm at scale magnification.

nodes.name: Planing machine (bed and tool)
nodes.note: Tool holder reciprocates on massive rigid base. Work bolted to moving table under tool. Cast-iron bed hand-scraped for parallelism and flatness to 1mm over metre length. Much heavier than lathe, needs water power. Now surfaces can be finished flat. Gap: no vertical motion yet.

nodes.name: Profile projector for large-scale part checking
nodes.note: Lens projects magnified shadow (50x to 200x) onto screen. Part mounted on XY stage accurate to 0.01mm. Operator aligns part against master profile drawn on screen. Faster than toolmaker's microscope for large parts, less accurate.

nodes.name: Reamer with multiple flutes
nodes.note: Four or six flutes; cutting edges at same diameter. Removes 0.05mm per side per pass. Produces finish accurate to 0.1mm on ID. Used after drill to reach tolerance. Machine reamer with back-taper prevents binding.

nodes.name: Roundness measurement without perfect reference
nodes.note: Part rotates on spindle (10 micron runout max). Dial indicator holds tip against surface as part turns. Mechanical filter (averaging arm) removes spindle runout, reading only part roundness error. Requires knowledge that runout and roundness are separable.

nodes.name: Hand-scraped surface plate and why it beats grinding
nodes.note: Scraper removes 0.002-inch (50 micron) peaks by hand, leaving high spots touching across area. Flatness reaches 0.05mm over metre. Grinding the same size plate requires weeks; hand scraping requires weeks but leaves damping-friendly rough surface. Machine slides run smoother and quieter on scraped surfaces.

nodes.name: Shaper machine with quick-return mechanism
nodes.note: Crank-driven tool bar moves in short stroke, cutting on extension only. Quick-return allows work positioning during return. Whitworth linkage or Hydraulic feed enables vertical and horizontal capability on same machine. Smaller footprint than planer, hence more popular. Enables T-slots and pockets.

nodes.name: Sine bar and sine plate for angle measurement
nodes.note: Steel bar with two precision cylinders at known distance (5 or 10 inches). Tilting it onto gauge blocks sets angle via simple trigonometry. Enables angle grinding and gear pitch to 0.1 degrees. Accuracy requires gauge blocks.

nodes.name: Simple slide rest on lathe bed
nodes.note: Carriage slides on bed Ways are hand-scraped flat and parallel to 1mm. Lead screw (from master_screw) drives longitudinal feed. Tool holder is hand-clamped on cross-slide. Now a human can feed accurately without constant hand-jiggling. Enables repeatable diameters to 1mm.

nodes.name: Slotter machine for keyways and slots
nodes.note: Vertical tool bar reciprocates. Rotary table beneath allows indexing work for slots and keyways. Precision of slot depth depends on stop blocks accurate to 0.1mm. Enables gearbox internals and shaft-coupling slots. More specialised than shaper.

nodes.name: Reference square derived from plane
nodes.note: Plane sole determines angle to 0.05 degrees via scraping. Steel blade face and stem form square's working edge. Tested by rotation on surface plate: blade and plate contact all around. Enables perpendicularity checking.

nodes.name: Standard metre and wavelength of light standard
nodes.note: Platinum standard metre bar defines length. Later: wavelength of red Cd light = 643.847 nm = definition of metre. Moves definition from object to phenomenon. Enables every lab to define length without artifact reference. Changes metrology from physics-of-things to physics-of-light.

nodes.name: Straightedge and reference straightness
nodes.note: Cast-iron bar hand-scraped flat within 0.05mm over metre length. Light falls through 0.1mm gap if not in contact. Essential reference tool. Worn straightedges become rounded and measure optimistically: must be checked against other straightedges in rotation.

nodes.name: Surface grinder with reciprocating electromagnet
nodes.note: Rotating abrasive wheel at 1500-3000 rpm feeds into work on moving table. Electromagnet holds ferrous work. Enables finish to 0.01mm (10 microns). Wheel must be balanced and trued, else vibration ruins finish. Requires cap_tol_10um table motion.

nodes.name: Tailstock and dead centre
nodes.note: Tailstock slides along bed and clamped in position; dead centre (hardened point) supports work end without rotation. Conical fit and hand-scraped fit require cap_tol_1mm. Axial runout then limited by lathe spindle.

nodes.name: Taps and dies with thread standards
nodes.note: Whitworth thread (55-degree, interchangeable with sizes) costs little to standardize. Hand tap cuts internal thread; die cuts external. Both must be hard (hardened steel 50 Rc+) and accurate 0.05mm pitch. Huge cost benefit: parts interchangeable, no custom threads per customer.

nodes.name: Three-wire method for screw thread pitch diameter
nodes.note: Three hardened cylinders positioned in thread grooves (two on bottom, one on top). Vernier measures distance across wires. Simple algebra (lookup table) converts to pitch diameter. More robust than pitch micrometer. Enables Whitworth thread verification.

nodes.name: Tool and cutter grinder for milling tool angles
nodes.note: Grinding wheel at multiple indexable angles grinds rake, relief, lip, and spiral angles into milling tools. Requires angle measurement to 0.5 degrees and radial feed to 0.01mm. Masters the milling industry.

nodes.name: Tool steel, high speed steel, carbide and cutting speed gains
nodes.note: Tool steel (plain carbon): 20 m/min on cast iron. HSS (W, V, Cr, Co): 40 m/min, withstands red hardness. Carbide (WC + binder): 200 m/min, but brittle and hard to grind. Each step requires controlled hardening. Carbide demands carbide grinding wheel.

nodes.name: Toolmaker's microscope with precision stage
nodes.note: Compound microscope (50x) on XY stage with lead screws and vernier scales. Stage moves 0.01mm per vernier division. Enables measuring tool angles, pitch dimensions, and edge geometry. Combined with optical flat, verifies tool geometry to 1 micron.

nodes.name: Toolroom as institution and knowledge centre
nodes.note: Dedicated space for gauge making, jig design, machine maintenance. Master machinist leads apprentices. Teaches measurement, geometry, material properties. Institutional memory prevents tool designs being reinvented per factory. Concentrates capital in gauges rather than machinery.

nodes.name: Tracer lathe with hydraulic copying
nodes.note: Tracing stylus follows master contour. Hydraulic amplifier drives tool cross-feed. Operator controls longitudinal feed manually. Enables conical or curved lathe work (gun barrels, telescope tubes) without manual skill. Reduces labour but requires master casting per variant.

nodes.name: Treadle lathe with flywheel
nodes.note: The flywheel stores kinetic energy from foot pedal, giving continuous cutting rather than reciprocating bow drive. One person can now hold and feed work. Enables cam operation and steady-speed cutting.

nodes.name: Twist drill with helical flute
nodes.note: Helical flute evacutes chips from deep holes. Two-flute geometry creates cutting edges and flute valleys. Requires precise grind of point angle and lip relief. Invention is the flute clearance geometry, not the point. Enables deep, clean drilling.

nodes.name: Universal milling machine with tilting head and swivel table
nodes.note: Spindle tilts horizontally and vertically. Table swivels to any angle. Can mill helical flutes and angled teeth. Requires precision indexing to 0.1 degrees and feed positioning to 0.1mm. More versatile, hence more skilled operator required.

nodes.name: Vernier caliper with 0.05mm resolution
nodes.note: Sliding scale with 20 divisions over 19mm creates vernier effect: 1mm / 20 = 0.05mm readability. Requires master_screw precision on main scale and fine tooling on slave scale. Hand-readability plateaus at 0.05mm.

nodes.name: Chatter and self-excited vibration in machine tools
nodes.note: Cutting forces excite frame resonance. Tool marks on work regenerate at spindle frequency, reinforcing vibration. Chatter makes 0.1mm ripples, destroying tolerance. Solution: reduce depth-of-cut, increase speed (raises natural frequency), or damp frame. Theoretical explanation late 20th century.

nodes.name: True plane surfaces by the three-plate method
nodes.note: The foundation of everything mechanical, and it needs nothing Rome does not have. Two plates lapped together converge on a matched sphere and socket. Three plates lapped in rotation can only converge on flat. From the plane you derive the straightedge, the square, the gauge, the screw, and every machine after.

nodes.name: Movable type and the screw press
nodes.note: Rome already has the screw press for oil and wine, so half the machine exists. The hard parts are the punch-cut matrix, the adjustable hand mould for casting type at speed, and oil-based ink that will not bead on metal. Politically ambiguous: frame it as multiplying the classics, never as publishing. POLITICALLY AMBIGUOUS. Cheap accurate copying breaks the elite's control of what is known and by whom. Frame it as multiplying Homer, Virgil and the Twelve Tables, never as publishing. Print the classics first and visibly.

nodes.name: Calotype negative-positive
nodes.note: The negative is the invention. Paper negative allows unlimited prints from one exposure. Cheaper than daguerreotype.

nodes.name: Carbon ink
nodes.note: Lampblack or charcoal suspended in gum. For brush and reed pen on soft surfaces.

nodes.name: Cataloguing and classification
nodes.note: Systematic ordering by subject, author, title. Index cards or catalogue. Turns collection into resource.

nodes.name: Cinema projection
nodes.note: Arc lamp casts film frames through objective lens onto screen. Large bright image. Darkened theatre essential.

nodes.name: Cinema shutter
nodes.note: Rotating disc with opening blocks light during frame advance. Viewer sees each frame, not blur. Controls flicker.

nodes.name: Codex binding
nodes.note: Stacked pages sewn and bound. Replaces roll. Page finding is the real gain.

nodes.name: Colour photography
nodes.note: Multi-layer emulsion sensitive to red, green, blue. Complex chemistry. Colour casts and fading persist. Natural colour possible.

nodes.name: Composing stick and galley
nodes.note: Compositors set metal sorts in stick, proof, transfer to galley. Allows rearrangement before lock-up.

nodes.name: Copyright and publishing economics
nodes.note: Legal monopoly on copying enforces author and publisher income. Printing enables profitable copying.

nodes.name: Cylinder press
nodes.note: Rotating cylinder instead of platen. Type moves under rolling pressure. Faster, smoother. Steam power essential.

nodes.name: Daguerreotype plate
nodes.note: Polished copper plate, silver-coated, exposed to light, developed in mercury vapour. Mirror-like image. Cannot be copied.

nodes.name: Disc record and lateral recording
nodes.note: Groove meanders side-to-side encoding amplitude. Shellac pressing from master. Playable from multiple copies.

nodes.name: Electrical recording and amplification
nodes.note: Microphone captures sound, valve amplifier drives cutting stylus. Bass and treble accessible. Audio fidelity leap. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electrotype plate
nodes.note: Electroplated copper shell on lead backing. Sharper impression. More durable. Expensive. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Optical enlarger
nodes.note: Light projects negative through lens onto sensitised paper. Magnification variable. Enlargement unlocks full potential.

nodes.name: Etching with acid
nodes.note: Wax ground on copper, needle drawn, acid bites. Tonal work without hand-cutting. Faster than engraving.

nodes.name: Film studio and stage
nodes.note: Large glass-roofed stage with strong arc lighting. Actors repeat scenes for camera. Raw material for film assembly.

nodes.name: Four-colour separation
nodes.note: Cyan, magenta, yellow, black separations photographed through filters. Overprinted recreate full colour.

nodes.name: Fourdrinier papermaking machine
nodes.note: Steam-driven endless wire belt. Pulp fed continuously. Thousands of tonnes per year. Displaces hand workers.

nodes.name: Gelatin dry plate
nodes.note: Silver halide in gelatin. Sensitive when dry. Long shelf life. Easy storage and transport. Portable photography practical.

nodes.name: Halftone screening
nodes.note: THE invention making photographs printable. Cross-ruled screen photographed with image. Variable dots create tone illusion.

nodes.name: Adjustable hand mould
nodes.note: Iron mould with adjustable sides, matrix fitted into bottom. One caster casts thousands of identical sorts per day.

nodes.name: Hand papermaking
nodes.note: Rag fibre beaten, suspended in water, scooped on mould. One sheet at a time. Variable thickness.

nodes.name: Index and concordance
nodes.note: Complete list of every word and location. Enables rapid lookup and cross-reference. Transforms corpus to reference.

nodes.name: Intaglio engraving
nodes.note: Furrows cut into copper plate. Ink fills grooves, wiped surface clean. Pressure forces paper into grooves. Fine detail.

nodes.name: Intermittent film movement
nodes.note: Sprockets and claw mechanism pull film frame-by-frame. Each frame holds still, advances in darkness. THE invention of cinema.

nodes.name: Library and archive
nodes.note: Institutional preservation and organisation of texts. Enables distributed knowledge and cultural memory.

nodes.name: Linotype machine
nodes.note: Operator taps keyboard, matrices drop, spacing added, hot metal poured into mould. Complete line emerges cast solid.

nodes.name: Lithography
nodes.note: Greasy ink on stone, water-acidified alum applied. Water repels grease, grease rejects water. Non-obvious chemistry.

nodes.name: Loudspeaker
nodes.note: Coil in magnetic field vibrates diaphragm. Reverses microphone. Weak signal amplified for audible volume.

nodes.name: Magic lantern projection
nodes.note: Candle or arc light projects painted glass slide through lens onto screen. Bright large image. Enables mass viewing.

nodes.name: Magnetic wire and tape recording
nodes.note: Steel wire or tape magnetised by recording head. Erasable and reusable. Linear response superior to disc.

nodes.name: Monotype machine
nodes.note: Punched paper tape controls type casting. Each character cast individually. Slower than Linotype but flexible fonts.

nodes.name: Mosaic and fresco
nodes.note: Permanent architectural image. Tesserae or pigment in plaster. Not reproducible.

nodes.name: Newspaper institution
nodes.note: Daily publication breaks state monopoly on information. Political instrument. Cheap accurate copying enables rapid idea spread.

nodes.name: Nitrate film storage safety
nodes.note: Nitrocellulose base extremely flammable and self-oxidising. Fires spontaneous and unstoppable. Underground vaults needed.

nodes.name: Offset lithography
nodes.note: Image transfers to rubber roller, then paper. Multiple passes with less wear. Finer detail, longer plate life.

nodes.name: Oil-based printing ink
nodes.note: Carbon in heated linseed oil. Sticks to metal type. Water-based ink beads off metal, non-obvious blocker.

nodes.name: Papyrus sheets
nodes.note: Rome has abundant supply from Egypt. Writing surface, not an invention.

nodes.name: Parchment sheets
nodes.note: Rome produces from animal skin. Durable, reusable, erasable, expensive.

nodes.name: Phonograph with cylinder
nodes.note: Sound vibrates needle, etches waxy cylinder. Replay moves needle over groove, vibrates diaphragm. Sound reproduction.

nodes.name: Platen press
nodes.note: Flat bed with screwed platen pressing it down. Requires oil ink and level surfaces. Gutenberg innovation.

nodes.name: Water-driven pulp stamper
nodes.note: Water wheel drives cam-driven hammers beating rags. Faster, consistent pulp. Essential for volume.

nodes.name: Radio broadcasting as medium
nodes.note: Sound broadcast live to distant unseen audiences. Electrical medium dissolves geography. State interest high.

nodes.name: Relief printing
nodes.note: Ink raised surface, press down. Works with carbon ink and soft brush on absorbent surface.

nodes.name: Roll film on celluloid
nodes.note: Flexible base allows compact cameras. Light and durable. Enables hand-held shooting. Photography becomes casual.

nodes.name: Rotary press
nodes.note: Two cylinders, type wraps around curved plate. Continuous feed and output. Thousands of sheets per hour.

nodes.name: Scribal copying
nodes.note: Trained hand copying, one manuscript at a time. Elite control of knowledge.

nodes.name: Sculpture
nodes.note: Stone or bronze permanent image. Single work, not reproducible.

nodes.name: Seals and stamps
nodes.note: Hand-carved into stone, metal or bone. Verify identity and authenticity.

nodes.name: Silver halide chemistry
nodes.note: Silver nitrate and sodium chloride form photosensitive silver chloride crystals. Darkens on exposure. Foundation of photography. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Surface sizing
nodes.note: Alum and gelatin seal fibre. Ink sits on surface instead of bleeding through. Required for printing.

nodes.name: Stereotype plate
nodes.note: Plaster impression of type. Molten type poured into mould. Reusable, faster than resetting type.

nodes.name: Theatre and pantomime
nodes.note: Live performance of narrative. Ephemeral, audience present, not reproducible.

nodes.name: Type matrix
nodes.note: Soft brass struck by hardened punch. Cavity is negative of letter. Reusable mould for casting type.

nodes.name: Type metal alloy
nodes.note: Lead and tin melt at low temp. Antimony is key: it expands on cooling, forcing alloy into matrix cavity edge. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Type punch
nodes.note: Hardened steel letter in relief, hand-struck into soft matrix. Repeated use creates identical matrices.

nodes.name: Typewriter
nodes.note: Keyed strike-through ribbon. QWERTY deliberately slows typist to prevent jams. Shift key accesses capitals.

nodes.name: Wax tablets
nodes.note: Wooden frames with wax layer. Reusable by heating. For notes, not archival.

nodes.name: Wet collodion plate
nodes.note: Glass plate coated with collodion. Exposed wet. Huge leap in sensitivity and speed. Must develop within minutes.

nodes.name: Wire mould and deckle
nodes.note: Fine brass wire mesh and wooden deckle frame. Allows consistent sheet thickness. Wire spacing visible.

nodes.name: Wood pulp from timber
nodes.note: Wood fibres liberated by heat and alkali. Cheaper than rag pulp. Contains lignin, yellows and becomes brittle.

nodes.name: Woodblock carving
nodes.note: Hand-carved relief block prints many copies. First cheap reproducible image. Breaks scribe monopoly.

nodes.name: Animal-driven treadmill
nodes.note: Ox or horse walks inside a large wheel to power mill machinery or pumps. Available wherever you have animals; used at Roman mines.

nodes.name: Cornish boiler
nodes.note: One large fire tube through the water. Rugged, handles high pressure, but prone to violent failure if the tube plugs and overheats. Requires skilled operation and routine inspection. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Haystack boiler
nodes.note: A rounded iron shell, fire at the bottom, the simplest boiler. Low pressure, small explosion risk, but slow steam generation and poor heat transfer. Used where durability matters more than speed. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Lancashire boiler
nodes.note: Two fire tubes: more heat surface than Cornish, better steam generation. Smaller diameter tubes cool faster if they scale, less dramatic failure. Industrial standard for textile mills and pumping stations. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Wagon boiler
nodes.note: Cylindrical shell, internal fire tubes passing through water. More surface area than haystack; faster steam generation. Mobile, used on early locomotives and threshing machines. Prone to scale and tube fouling. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Water-tube boiler
nodes.note: Small tubes of water through a chamber of hot gas, boiler in a steel frame. Much higher steam generation than fire-tube types, safer (small volume of water means less explosive stored energy), but more complex assembly and maintenance.

nodes.name: Breastshot waterwheel
nodes.note: Water hits the wheel at mid-height, between overshot and undershot. Smeaton measured efficiency systematically: breastshot wins by combining gravity and impulse when head is moderate. This is how empirical engineering began.

nodes.name: Cable tool drilling (percussion drilling)
nodes.note: A steam engine drives a walking beam; a heavy chisel on a cable strikes repeatedly, shattering rock. Bailing removes cuttings and water. Works deep and slow; no rotary motion needed. The first practical oil drilling method. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Coal gas and gasworks
nodes.note: Heating coal in a retort produces flammable gases: hydrogen, methane, carbon monoxide. These can be piped and burned for light and heat. The tar and ammonia are byproducts; sulfur stinks and corrodes. Early gasworks are small; scaling needs chemistry.

nodes.name: Coal seam and mining
nodes.note: Coal is buried stone that burns: anthracite in deep seams. Mining requires shoring and drainage. Early mines are shallow; deep coal demands ventilation and pumping to stay safe and dry.

nodes.name: Coking: coal to coke
nodes.note: Heating coal without air produces coke (carbon) and coal tar. Coke is almost pure carbon: hotter burning, less ash and sulfur than coal. Essential for iron smelting at scale in a blast furnace. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Condenser and vacuum
nodes.note: A chamber cooled by circulating water, condensing exhaust steam into liquid. This creates a vacuum, pulling the piston back harder, doubling engine power. The cooling water must be copious and clean; copper tubing survives longer than iron. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Electric motor and end of line shafting
nodes.note: Individual electric motors at each machine, replacing the central steam engine and line shafting running through the factory. This is a larger productivity gain than any single machine: workers control their own pace, maintenance is local, floor space opens up.

nodes.name: Feedwater heater and economiser
nodes.note: Hot exhaust gas preheats incoming cold water in an economiser; hot condensate is also reused. This cuts fuel consumption significantly. Requires careful design to avoid scale and tube plugging. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Flywheel and governor
nodes.note: The flywheel stores rotary energy, smoothing the lumpy strokes of a reciprocating engine. A centrifugal governor with weighted arms adjusts throttle, keeping speed steady despite changing load. Watt's great innovation.

nodes.name: Flywheel energy storage
nodes.note: A massive disc or wheel, spun up and allowed to coast. Energy is stored as rotary momentum. Used in pumping stations to store water-mill power and release it on demand, or to smooth reciprocating engine output. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Force pump
nodes.note: Roman force pumps lift water by mechanical displacement, not by suction alone. Critical for aqueducts and mines; requires a slave or animal to operate.

nodes.name: Fuel cell (hydrogen-oxygen)
nodes.note: Hydrogen and oxygen react at separate electrodes in an electrolyte, producing DC directly. Efficient, silent, no heat loss, but hydrogen is expensive to produce. Grove and Schönbein discovered it in the 1840s; Grove built a telegraph powered by fuel cells. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Fuel oil (heavy fraction)
nodes.note: Heavy oil from the still bottom: too thick to burn in lamps, but a boiler fuel for ships and stationary engines. Higher energy density than coal by weight; viscous, needing heating to flow and atomization to burn. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Gas engine and internal combustion
nodes.note: Coal gas is sucked in, mixed with air, sparked, and exploded. Much lighter and simpler than a steam engine. No boiler, no furnace, no engineer. Otto and Diesel engines follow. Early models are unreliable; ignition is the problem. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Gas main and gas network
nodes.note: Seamless iron pipe laid underground, distribution on a town or city scale. Requires precision joints, testing for leaks, and reliable supply. Gas is lighter than air: pipes must slope and have drains for condensed tar.

nodes.name: Gas meter
nodes.note: A wet meter with pistons in a sealed chamber, gas pushing them round, a dial recording revolutions. Charges customers fairly and identifies leaks. Requires careful assembly and sealed joints.

nodes.name: High voltage transmission
nodes.note: Power loss in a wire is proportional to I squared; raising voltage and lowering current for the same power reduces losses dramatically. Remote hydro becomes economic only with high voltage. Requires transformers, insulators, and careful design.

nodes.name: Hydroelectric power station
nodes.note: A dam, penstock, turbine, and dynamo coupled: water flow becomes rotary motion becomes electrical current. The scale is decided by head and flow. Long-distance transmission at high voltage makes remote hydro economical.

nodes.name: Indicator diagram (Watt's instrument)
nodes.note: A small pump coupled to the engine cylinder; a pencil draws a closed curve on a moving drum of paper. The area inside is work; the height is pressure. This turns thermodynamics from guessing into measurement: you can see what the engine actually does.

nodes.name: Kerosene (paraffin) lamps
nodes.note: Kerosene is a clear liquid fraction with a clean flame, brighter than candles or whale oil. Cheaper to refine than to ship coal. Lamps are simple: wick, chimney, brass fitting. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Lead-acid storage battery
nodes.note: Lead oxide and lead plates in sulfuric acid: charge with DC, discharge to get power. Rechargeable, robust, stores significant energy. The acid eats organic matter and corrodes copper; wood cases and lead terminals are necessary. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Leat and weir
nodes.note: The leat is a conduit bringing water from higher up the valley, often in an aqueduct on stonework or timber. The weir diverts water from the river. Together they concentrate flow and head at the mill site.

nodes.name: Load factor and grid economics
nodes.note: Load factor is average demand over peak demand. A grid with high load factor is economical: fixed costs (wires, transformers) are spread over more revenue. Time-of-use tariffs and reservoir storage improve load factor.

nodes.name: Millpond and storage
nodes.note: A dam and reservoir upstream of the mill, holding water during low flow, releasing it when needed. This gives you power when the stream does not: seasonal agriculture, milling, mining.

nodes.name: Nickel-iron battery
nodes.note: Nickel oxide and iron electrodes in caustic soda solution. Tougher than lead-acid, tolerates abuse and overcharge, but lower voltage and self-discharge. Edson and Tesla championed it; it is still used in harsh environments. [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Horizontal waterwheel (Norse)
nodes.note: The rotor spins on a vertical axis, driven by a direct vertical jet. No complex gearing needed, no right-angle transmission. Rugged, efficient for small streams with drop.

nodes.name: Nuclear fission and power
nodes.note: Honest assessment: nuclear power requires uranium enrichment to weapons-grade purity (99.9999+%), neutron physics at a level unknown to Rome, materials research for radiation damage, and a national security programme. The reactor is the easy part. Start this only if you have a state programme with decades and billions to spare.

nodes.name: Oil refinery and distillation
nodes.note: Crude oil boils at different temperatures; fractional distillation separates light fractions (petrol, kerosene) from heavy (fuel oil, tar). Requires large copper stills, careful heating control, and condensers. The fractions are products, not wastes.

nodes.name: Oil shale and bitumen deposits
nodes.note: Oil shale and bitumen seeps exist; heating shale gives a bituminous liquid. The yield is poor and transport is heavy, but it is available without drilling if you find the deposits.

nodes.name: Overshot waterwheel
nodes.note: Rome has this too, notably the 16-wheel Barbegal complex. Weight of the water does the work; it needs a significant drop but delivers more power per wheel.

nodes.name: Peat extraction and burning
nodes.note: Bog digging gives you fuel where forest is scarce. Peat burns slower and wetter than wood but is abundant in northern Europe. Not Rome's world yet, but available in the North.

nodes.name: Pelton wheel
nodes.note: A jet of water hits a double-cup bucket at high speed, splitting the jet tangentially to the wheel. Ideal for very high heads with low flow. The bucket profile is critical; casting is easier than machining but requires controlled cooling to avoid cracks.

nodes.name: Petroleum seeps and collection
nodes.note: Oil seeps from rock faces and pools in low ground. Early collection by bucket and pit. No pressure, no depth, just ambient flow. Pitch, naphtha, light oil; use depends on locality. [AUDIT: capability prerequisite(s) cap_tol_100um were inferred by rome/sim/treetool.py repair, not stated by the author. Treat them as a floor, not a specification.] [AUDIT: State interest and suspicion were unset and have been defaulted from the category.]

nodes.name: Oil pipeline
